Would steel bullets travel faster than lead bullets?

Energy of a bullet is determined by its mass and velocity. A lower mass bullet will travel faster. All things equal, normally this is compensated by simply making the bullet bigger, thereby increasing the mass of the bullet. But, because of size and powder constraints it may not be possible to increase the size of a steel bullet enough to compensate for the loss of mass caused by the change of materials.

Sabot rounds work to dramatically increase velocity with a reduced bullet mass (lower mass with much higher velocity). Done properly out of an appropriate barrel it's possible to get a net energy benefit for the bullet plus flatter trajectories. Higher velocities tend to increase accuracy as less time in flight means less environmental influence.

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sabot

In general the material doesn't really matter so long as you're not up against physical constraints for the bullet and weapon. Where the material matters the most is upon impact. Higher mass bullets, because of inertia, will want to keep penetrating moreso than a lower mass yet faster bullet. But as you can see from the sabots there are tricks to be played here by material science and known targets (example, armor). Inversely, a super fast yet tiny bullet is more likely to pass through a body with limited damage simply because it does not have the time inside the body to impart much energy. It's the effective ability to impart (transfer) energy from the bullet to the target which causes damage. edit: Or in the case of hollow points, mushrooming.
